To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thermal neutron captureγ-ray spectrum of58Ni is dominated by the 8999 keV transition to the ground state in59Ni, while in the case of60Ni the 7837 keV transition to ground state in61Ni dominates the spectrum.
we measured the γ-ray spectra of the thermal neutron capture in 58Ni and 60Ni and derived the neutron binding energies Bn(59Ni)=8995(23) kev and Bn(60Ni)=7820(20) kev.

the neutron binding energies of59Ni and 61Ni were determined as 8999.15 (23) keV for 59Ni and 7820.07 (20) keV for61Ni, and that the γ-ray strength functions of both isotopes are similar to those of the neighboring even-even isotopes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neutron-captureγ-ray spectroscopy and the level density of59Ni and 61Ni.
the neutron captureγ-ray strength function, level density, and level scheme of59,61Ni.
the determination of the neutron capture cross-sections of the isotopes of the elements 57 and 59.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present data are in excellent agreement with all the previous experimental results and the theoretical predictions.
the level density parameter is a smooth function of the neutron number, but that the strength of the primary transitions depends strongly on the neutron number.
the level density parameter of59Ni, which is the most abundant Ni isotope, is not yet known with sufficient accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level density parameter a=0.12 A5/3 is confirmed and the primaryγ-strength function is found to be consistent with a Porter-Thomas distribution.
the neutron binding energies andγ-ray strength functions are in good agreement with theoretical predictions.

the experimental results are consistent with the statistical model predictions, except for a possible systematic deviation of the primary strength function from the predictions of a simple Weisskopf estimate.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a high-resolution γ-ray spectroscopic method, which is sensitive to small amounts of the isotope of interest, can be used to determine the neutron binding energy with a high accuracy, which in turn can be used to improve the accuracy of the determination of the neutron binding energy of the isotope.
the level density parameter is significantly higher than predicted by the standard back-shifted Fermi gas model.
the γ-ray strength function of primary transitions can be well reproduced by the statistical theory of nuclear reactions if the level density parameter is chosen to be 0.1 A-1/3.
